diagnosis_explanation:
Your main problem is pain in the upper belly. Doctors also think you may have a stomach problem. They also looked at your heart.

Your heart was not pumping as well as it should. This caused fluid to build up. Doctors worked to get the fluid out. You have a small amount of fluid around your heart sac. It is not causing problems.

You also have a thyroid problem. Your body needs this gland to work right. You have low potassium levels. Your body needs potassium to work well.

Doctors also looked at a spot in your brain. They are not sure if it is from a past heart attack or something else. You have had heart vessels opened before.
medication_rationale:
Coreg 12.5 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps your heart beat slower.
It also lowers your blood pressure.
This helps your heart need less oxygen.
You may feel tired or dizzy. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you get very dizzy.
Also call if your heart beats too slowly.

Cozaar 50 mg daily:
This medicine lowers your blood pressure.
It helps blood flow more freely.
This can help your heart work better.
You might feel dizzy at first.
Call your doctor if you feel faint.
Your skin or eyes might turn yellow.

Aldactone 25 mg daily:
This medicine helps your body get rid of salt.
It also helps your body keep potassium.
This can help lower your blood pressure.
You may need to urinate more often.
Call your doctor if you get muscle cramps.
Also call if you feel weak.

Synthroid 0.075 mg daily:
This medicine gives your body thyroid hormone.
Your thyroid gland might not make enough.
This helps your body's energy and metabolism.
You may feel more energetic.
Call your doctor if your heart beats very fast.
Also call if you feel nervous or shaky.

Carafate 1 gram 4 times a day:
This medicine coats your stomach lining.
It helps protect your stomach from acid.
This can help heal pain or sores in your stomach.
You may get constipated.
Call your doctor if your bowel movements change a lot.

Claritin 10 mg daily:
This medicine is an antihistamine.
It helps relieve allergy symptoms.
It can help with itching or hives.
You may feel drowsy.
This is a common side effect.

Lasix 20 mg daily:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra fluid.
This can lower blood pressure and help your heart.
You will urinate more often. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you feel dizzy.
Also call if you get muscle cramps.
Call your doctor if your heart beats too fast.

K-Dur 20 mEq daily:
This medicine gives your body potassium.
Your body may lose potassium with other medicines.
Potassium is important for your muscles and nerves.
You may have an upset stomach.
Call your doctor if you get chest pain.
Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Prilosec 40 mg daily:
This medicine reduces the acid in your stomach.
This can help relieve stomach pain.
It helps your stomach lining heal.
You may get a headache.
This is a common side effect.
Call your doctor if your stomach pain gets worse.

Zofran 4 mg every 4-6 hours as needed:
This medicine helps stop nausea and vomiting.
It works by affecting signals in your brain.
You may feel constipated.
This is a common side effect.
Call your doctor if you get a headache.
Also call if you feel dizzy.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore from your surgery.
- Focus on resting and short, slow walks inside your home.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Eat small, bland meals. Avoid spicy or fatty foods.
- Your goal this week is to walk to your mailbox and back.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Call your doctor if you have severe belly pain.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to feel a little better each day.
- You can slowly increase your walking distance indoors.
- Continue to avoid lifting anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Stick to bland foods. Your stomach is still healing.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your house several times a day.
- Call your doctor if you feel very sick to your stomach.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

**Week 3:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy this week.
- You can try walking a little outside if the weather is nice.
- Keep avoiding lifting heavy things. This is very important.
- You can start to try some regular foods but avoid spicy ones.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes without stopping.
- Call your doctor if your belly pain gets worse.
- Call your doctor if you have redness or swelling at your incision sites.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel more comfortable and have more energy.
- You can do light chores like folding laundry.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds this week.
- You can eat most regular foods, but listen to your stomach.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes outside each day.
- Call your doctor if you feel dizzy or faint.
- Call your doctor if your heart beats very fast.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people start to feel much better after 4 to 6 weeks.
- Keep following the activity and food guidance.
- Your doctor will check your heart function again soon.
- Slowly increase your activity as you feel stronger.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- You cannot catch your breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Face drooping or arm weakness: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that won't stop: You are losing too much blood.
- Sudden severe head pain: This could be a brain bleed.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Your brain is not getting blood.
- Seizure that is not stopping: Your brain is not working right.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Epigastric pain getting worse: This may be your heart or stomach.
- Confusion or disorientation: Your brain is not working right.
- Swelling in one leg with pain: This could be a blood clot.
- Cannot keep any fluids down: You are getting too dehydrated.
- Fever over 101 degrees F: You may have a bad infection.
- Vomiting blood or black stuff: You may be bleeding inside.
- Fall with head injury or pain: You could be hurt badly.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild stomach pain that is not bad: This can happen as you heal.
- Questions about your potassium pill: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Feeling tired or low energy: Your thyroid may need checking.
- Mild swelling in your legs: This can happen with heart problems.
